Watch out, coders -- a robot may take your job, too

While i think this is possible, I think coders will be the very last to be automated away, mainly because they take the abstract and translate it into logic. Mindless jobs like flipping burgers can easily be done by robots because the operations are not very abstract, they're almost formulaic, something easily implemented as a logic flow. The problems faced & solved by coders are so varied and so different on a case to case basis, it's not as easy to replace without a working mind behind the issue.

The "robots" won't take coders jobs any time soon, but they make them easier through macros, code generators and learning algorythms. Coding is for a big part creative work and that's something AI can't do (yet?).
You might want to take a look at Emily Howell. Admitelly songwriting is far from codewroting, but it's a first step.

Copying a comment I made a while back on Plebbit:

"At least for the "Emily Howell" example, while it is pretty nice music, there's nothing really special about it. Music can be very mathematical if you want it to be. Specific notes go together well, certain chords feel like a start or end, and so on. The music created by that particular AI is certainly indistinguishable from man made music, but it's very simple mathematical music that was made to sound good. It's the same way they churn out chart-topping pop hits, the only difference is that people make it. All the music that it made was simple, short, one instrument pieces that weren't particularly complicated or moving. A lot of music often uses "pleasing dissonance" that isn't really something a formula can follow. Use it in the wrong way or time and it just sounds like crap, and is very subjective. Just look at guitar distortion. It shouldn't sound good, but it does.

I'll be impressed by it when they have AI that can create something beyond piano, say an entire symphony or rock band. I'll be impressed when the AI can capture the feel of an era, or write some shitty protest song. I'll be impressed when AI can find or create some new instrument and create entire new genres. I'll be impressed when AI becomes the next biggest thing out of their parent's garage.

There's still a lot to go in the way of making AI music, and I can't really see it going beyond maybe making the standard top 40 pop hits. Even then, however, they'll need someone to sing the songs. Voice synthesis still sounds terrible, I'd hate to hear synthesized singing.

Maybe I'm just deluding myself, though. I hope not. Call me whatever you want, but I don't want to live in a world where everything is spoon-fed to me by robots, all designed and programmed for my optimum enjoyment."
